human_tolerance.notes: It is one of the commonest birds in urban parks, willow thickets and suburban areas across the northern United States and southern Canada, and it nests readily in suburban tree cavities and nest boxes.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Pairs are formed in late autumn and winter and the winter flocks disperse into those pairs in spring; a clutch of six to eight eggs is laid and incubated by the female alone for 11 to 14 days.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Outside the breeding season birds join mixed-species flocks, which form because chickadees call out whenever they find a good source of food; the diet shifts to seeds and berries.

vocalizations.description: Two clear whistles, the second about a third higher than the first. The song typically starts around 400 Hz with tones spanning roughly 1 kHz, and males sing it only in relative isolation from other chickadees.

The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call, produced by both sexes year round. The number of dee notes tracks the level of threat: usually two, but four or more for a serious threat, and one recorded warning about a pygmy owl carried 23 dees. Other species in a mixed flock respond to it.
A gargle noise used by males as a threat of attacking another male, often when feeding, and also in sexual contexts; chicks learn it soon after birth.

range.note: 'Black-capped chickadees are non-migratory and can be found throughout much of North America... from western Alaska, through southern Yukon and throughout the Canadian provinces, from British Columbia in the west to the Maritimes', with the northern United States in the southern part of that range. Mexico is not in the range and is left off.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'The birds hop along tree branches searching for food, sometimes hanging upside down or hovering; they may make short flights to catch insects in the air.'

traits.nest_type.note: 'The black-capped chickadee nests in tree cavities 1-7 m above ground.'

traits.length_m.note: The article gives no total length, only the male wing length of 63.5-67.5 mm and tail length of 58-63 mm. 0.14 m is derived from those two midpoints (65.5 mm and 60.5 mm) plus roughly 20 mm for the head projecting past the folded wing, which is how a small passerine's total length relates to its two longest measured segments. It is an estimate, not a sourced total length.

traits.wingspan_m.note: The article gives no wingspan. 0.19 m is estimated from the male wing length of 63.5-67.5 mm, taken as about 1.4 wing chords for a short, round-winged passerine of this size. It is an estimate, not a sourced measurement.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Maximum recorded lifespan is 12 years, although most live roughly 2.5 years.' The record is the mean most birds attain.

traits.diet.note: 'Insects (especially caterpillars) form a large part of their diet in summer' and 'seeds and berries' are taken in winter; the article's summary calls the diet primarily insects and seeds. Shares are a judgement.

traits.social.note: 'mixed species flocks may form to help with foraging and predator avoidance' with nuthatches, woodpeckers, kinglets and virees, and the flock disperses into pairs in spring; the group-size range is a judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: The fee-bee song is sung by males during the breeding season and both sexes call year round; day activity follows from a bird that forages by sight along branches and calls to hold a flock together.

traits.defense.note: The chick-a-dee-dee-dee call is an alarm call whose number of dees reports the threat level, and other species respond to it; the bird's response to a threat is to signal and move rather than to attack.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: it lives in urban parks and suburban areas and comes readily to a hand-held seed.

habitat.use.note: 'Black-capped chickadees inhabit wooded areas, including both coniferous and deciduous forests, urban parks, willow thickets, and suburban areas' and they forage along branches; a strongly arboreal split is a judgement from that.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: It nests and roosts in tree cavities 1-7 m up; 'cavity' is the matching drawable shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Insect- and seed-dominated diet, cavity nesting, dense vegetation for cover and perching; weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'urban parks, willow thickets, and suburban areas' are named explicitly.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Black-capped chickadees are non-migratory', with only 'irregular bird migration and dispersal' in winter.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Follows from the species being non-migratory: the whole population stays.

seasonal.phases.note: 'Black-capped chickadees start to form breeding pairs in the late fall and into the winter. In the spring, the winter flocks will disperse into the constituent pairs' and the winter diet shifts to seeds; the exact calendar windows here are a judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'there are usually six to eight eggs', 'Incubation lasts 11-14 days and is by the female only', and 'Young leave the nest 12-16 days after hatching, in great part because the parents start presenting food only outside the nest hole.' 14 days is the midpoint of the sourced nestling period; the 0.8 scale is a judgement.

vocalizations.fee_bee.note: 'One of the most recognizable sounds produced, particularly by the males, is the two-note fee-bee whistle'; 'the frequency of their songs typically starts around 400 Hz, and various tones spanning roughly 1 kHz are sung within the song'; and 'the males sing the song only in relative isolation from other chickadees'.

vocalizations.chickadee_dee.note: 'The most familiar call is the chick-a-dee-dee-dee, which gave this bird its name... produced by both males and females year-round', and 'the number of dees indicates the level of threat from nearby predators', with 23 dees recorded in one warning about a pygmy owl.

vocalizations.gargle.note: 'Black-capped chickadees make a number of other calls and sounds, such as a gargle noise usually used as a threat of attacking another male, often when feeding. This call is also used in sexual contexts', and it is learned soon after birth.

look.note: 'The black-capped chickadee has a black cap and bib with white cheeks. Its underparts are white with buff-coloured flanks. Its back is unstreaked and greenish grey, and the tail and wings are slate grey. It has a black beak and legs, and dark brown irises.' Palette, proportions and box placement are judgement; the bib is drawn on the breast.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program, with the fee-bee whistle standing in for song and insects as the food tag.
